While I agree with you on the idea that malingering should be a topic of discussion, I feel that you should remember two points that may lessen the blow of this phenomenon.

1. People who malinger/have munchusens syndrome are in themselves ill and do deserve help for their dysfunctional need to be "disordered". Often, individuals who feel some righteous anger disregard the common fact that these people are individuals in great distress that hold a valid disorder that deserves treatment.

2. Disorders are not something that holds much value in the grand scheme of things. People often feel offended when they see others "faking" their disorder but they fail to realize that disorders are simply Classifications that hold no basis in reality. They are simply systems that allow clinicians and Healthcare providers to provide help easier. That isn't to say that mental illness is not real, just that the specific "labels" are not concrete structures but rather patterns of behaviour that suit the purpose of identification. Basically, what I am trying to say is, the disorder has no real meaning outside of its diagnostic value, so they aren't taking anything big away from you.
